questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important that the country was English speaking so meeting new people and attending classes wouldn't be a problem in terms of language, Also, I looked for universities with good non-academic opportunities and read about Southampton from other students who went their on exhange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, it has been a really great experience going abroad, and I would recommend it to everyone! I really liked the campus, and most of my modules were really interesting. I met so many nice people, both locals and internationals and got to experience so many nice places around Southampton with them.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, I experienced some problems finding the information I was looking for, for example on the university's website. However, before arriving, I received the contact information of my personal academic tutor. He was very helpful and answered all my questions before my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university has a pick-up service, where they drive you from the airport to your accommodation. Since I lived in the University accommodation, bedding, and some kitchen utensils were provided. When I arrived at the hall, there was a team who welcomed me, showed me to my room and gave me some information about the accomendation, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I received my offer of accommodation late - less than 2 weeks before arriving. I tried to contact them but they didn't respond. When I received the offer, there was an error in the contract. Therefore I had to call them, but this was solved quickly and didn't experience any problems after this.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university has different halls around the city, primarily close to campus and some in between the city centre and campus, which was where I lived. I just applied through the university, which was an easy process. However, I talked with a lot of people who lived in private accommodation off-campus, who told me that it had been pretty easy to find as well. Also, the private accommodation was cheaper than the university halls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Since Southampton is not a very big city, you can live in the city and still not be that far away from campus. I lived in between and it took me around 15 min with the bus, or around 25/30 min to walk to school, which I think is nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it's nice that the university provides accommodation for their students. Also, when you live in the halls, you get a free bus card, which is really nice. However, the halls are more expensive than private accommodation, and if I would go there again, I would probably go for private accommodation since it was just as nice but less expensive. Also, it's very common for 1st-year students to live in the halls, therefore, most of my flatmates were around 18-19 years old and had never lived out before. The kitchen was often dirty since people easily forgot to clean after themselves, which was a bit annoying.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To be honest, I can't really remember the process that well, which must indicate that the process was pretty easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the course catalogue on the website and included the courses I wanted in a document that was sent to the university. Since I applied for a module in another faculty outside of psychology, I received an email that the administration had to find out whether it was possible for me to take the module, but in the end, I was allowed to take all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted my personal academic tutor, who was very helpful and answered all my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very successful since I got all the classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions, contact your personal academic tutor - maybe they don't have the answer, but then they can tell you who to contact.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academic opportunities weren't my primary reason for going abroad, and therefore I didn't have that many expectations. Although the level wasn't as high as at UCPH, I still learned a lot and found the academic program interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the modules were lectures and some prerecorded videos. I took a module in education, where the class was more of a seminar, which I really liked.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite different, for example, there wasn't a curriculum as we know it from home, but instead a list of recommended readings. Moreover, I think the focus was more on current research and not so much on theories. Also, the final grade was made up of different things, for example, quizzes, a presentation, research participation and an essay in the exam period.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Educational Psychology 
Current & Emerging Issues in Psycho-Oncology & Pain Research
Psychology of Attractiveness
Social Justice & Inclusive Education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Introduction to Educational Psychology and Social Justice & Inclusive Education, first and foremost because of the professors teaching the classes. The classes always covered intersting content, so I really liked going to them. I also liked Psychology of Attractiveness, because it was so different from the modules I have taken previously. The module covered why people fall in love, relationships, attraction etc. Also, the professor teaching the module is really great, and always included small, funny tasks for the students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since I received the bus card, I didn't have to spend money on transportation in Southampton. However, since I went on several trips and took the train, this was pretty expensive. Therefore, it's a good idea to buy a railcard, which gives you a discount on all your journeys. Also, I had to buy some kitchen equipment, since some were provided but not everything that I needed.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping and going out for dinner at restaurants and pubs was cheaper than in Denmark. The train was around the same as in Denmark, while housing (at least the Uni halls) was more expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The non-academic opportunities were great and were one of the main reasons why I chose to go to Southampton. There are so many clubs and societies, but also a gym, a pool, sports halls, and many different gym classes on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the university, there are more than 300 clubs and societies, which mean that there is something for everybody. For example, you can find creative-, cultural-, and sports clubs. At the beginning of the semester, there was an event, where the clubs members told about their clubs, which was a good way to hear about the many opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend joining some societies. This is a good way to make new friends and get to know the locals. I joined a sports society, and they had a training and a social event each week (for example going to a pub together), which is very common for societies. I found it nice that you try a new sport and get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try the local/English food at the pubs, go to a football match, take the train and explore the cities around Southampton - Bath, Brighton, Bournemouth, Isle of Wight etc. There are so many beautiful places to go, especially by the coast, where there are some really nice walks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! English people are very friendly and welcoming, and therefore it was easy to meet both locals and other exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the events at school (especially in the beginning of the semester), karaoke nights at the pub at campus, and joining a society

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are so nice and friendly, and very easy to talk to. I think that is very different from home, where most people never get to meet and talk with exchange students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1)Enjoy the campus experience and make the most of it by joining some societies and attending events at campus. 
2)I experienced the exam period to be harder than at home since the deadlines of the exams were very close to each other, so try to prepare for exams in advance to make the exam period less stressful. 
3)Explore the cities and nature around Southampton, often it's only 1-2 hours by train from the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many nice people, and get friends from different countries in Europe. It was also nice to try living and experiencing university in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think I would say that I experienced any greater challenges during my stay, but I guess it was a bit of a challenge, in the beginning, to adjust to the way of teaching and writing assignments since it was different from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
